Interface OidcClientSource

public interface OidcClientSource
Reads one relying party's registration, whole.

The seam between a provider endpoint and wherever registrations are kept — a secret store, a set of database tables, a static document. An implementation assembles whatever it reads into an OidcClientConfiguration: the client's own record, every endpoint it registers, and for each endpoint the credentials it accepts, the roles a request through it may act in, and the resources it may act on.

How long a registration stays cached, and whether it is cached at all, is an implementation's own. An endpoint reads through this on every request, so a source backed by something expensive to read is the one that decides what to do about it.

  • Method Details

    • client

      OidcClientConfiguration client(String clientId)
      Gets one relying party's registration.

      An unregistered client is one with nothing to read. An implementation may answer null or throw; an endpoint treats the two the same way, as a refusal indistinguishable from a client that never existed. A failure should not be cached, so a client registered a moment ago costs a fresh lookup rather than being refused until a cache expires.

      Parameters:
      clientId - requested client_id
      Returns:
      registration, or null if no client is registered under that ID
